text:
Jordan: heads-up from the release: a handful of customers reported regressions around long-polling timeouts, and PMs surfaced ~10 small UX asks from pilot customers. we need to decide: one focused hotfix squad or split bug + polish?

Mei: can we get severity counts? If timeouts cause customer jobs to fail, hotfix first.

Jordan: severity: 4 customers with failed background jobs (>=1 failure), 12 customers with increased API latency but retries succeed. Error rate bump ~1.1% at peak for streaming endpoints.

Rafael: sounds like hotfix-first. also suggest we limit context switch by making the polish squad async (owners but not full-time this week).

Claire: agree. polish items are mostly wording, small layout tweaks, and one onboarding flow change. estimate: 2 eng-days total if done by 1-2 part-timers.

Mei: hotfix plan outline: triage -> scoped patch (server-side timeout clamp + retry backoff smoothing) -> canary -> roll. runtime needs 3 engineer-days (profiling + patch + test). ops to provide canary pool.

deploy-bot: Canary pool request logged: pool-emb-cp-451. 3 GPUs, 8h window.

Jordan: proposal: 5-day micro-sprint. Day 0: triage + lock roadmap (freeze serving changes except hotfixes). Day 1-3: hotfix work + canary. Day 4: roll and quick polish sweep (owners complete their small tasks if green).

Rafael: acceptance criteria for hotfix: background job failure rate <=0.1% under synthetic load and 95th latency for long-polling below 300ms for 10k tokens in staging.

Claire: for polish: checklist under /docs/polish-checklist.md with items tagged low-effort. aim to close >=70% of polish list if hotfix passes.

Mei: freeze note: block merges touching serving_runtime and routing until hotfix passes CI + canary. allow docs/examples and small UI PRs to continue.

Jordan: decision recorded: hotfix-squad (Mei lead + 2 runtime engs), polish-surge (Claire lead, 2 part-timers). Ops to own canary and monitoring. I'll update roadmap and notify support/sales.

Rafael: canary steps (pinned in #eng-oncall):
```
1. deploy pool-emb-cp-451 as canary
2. route 3% traffic for 1h
3. run load scenario: ./perf/run_longpoll --tokens 10000 --qps 40 --duration 60m
4. collect metrics: p95_latency, job_failures, retry_rate
5. if job_failures=0 and p95 < 300ms for 45m -> escalate to 20% for 2h
```

deploy-bot: Canary created: canary-timeout-1801, alerts proxied to #eng-oncall and #support.

Claire: i'll publish the polish checklist and tag items as low/med/high effort; will only pick low-effort for micro-sprint.

Jordan: comms: tell affected customers: short note that we are deploying a targeted mitigation; ETA end of week. sales asked for a one-line blurb. draft: "We've identified and are deploying a mitigation for intermittent long-polling timeouts; we expect no disruption. Full perf follow-up will ship in next minor."

Mei: QA plan: 2h focused regression window during canary, then 1h smoke after roll. Rafael, can you own QA schedule?

Rafael: yes — allocating QA slot 14:00-16:00 Wed PST during canary. will post results in thread.

Jordan: if canary fails, fallbacks: revert to previous runtime build or enable conservative timeout guard. postmortem threshold: >0.5% job failures after 12h.

Claire: good. also adding polish owners to the sprint card so we don't lose those asks.

Mei: quick ask — tag any engineering changes with label:hotfix and reference this thread_ts for traceability.

Jordan: done. check-in tomorrow 09:30. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
